title: Post-combustion CO2 capture emissions-monitoring QA controls

sources.title: Post-combustion carbon dioxide capture: emerging techniques
Net Zero Teesside Power environmental permit variation application

facts.source_fact: Post-combustion capture plant is designed to maximise capture of CO2 for use or secure geological storage.
facts.expected_handling: Keep captured-CO2 destination and capture-system boundary explicit.

facts.source_fact: The guidance says plant design should aim for at least 95% CO2 capture during normal operating conditions.
facts.expected_handling: Treat 95% as a design aim under the guidance, not an automatically achieved measurement.

facts.source_fact: A design capture rate below 95% annual average normal-operation conditions requires justification such as cost-benefit evidence.
facts.expected_handling: Require documented justification for lower design rates.

facts.source_fact: Captured CO2 must meet transport and storage requirements including relevant impurity and water limits.
facts.expected_handling: Keep product-quality verification separate from capture-rate measurement.

facts.source_fact: PCC air-emission risks, including degradation products, require site-specific assessment and modelling to support permit limits.
facts.expected_handling: Carry modelling and permit provenance with ELVs.

facts.source_fact: The main monitoring purpose is to show process emissions, primarily to air, are not causing environmental harm.
facts.expected_handling: Do not reduce PCC monitoring to capture rate alone.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring must also demonstrate energy and resource efficiency.
facts.expected_handling: Keep energy/resource indicators distinct from emissions concentrations.

facts.source_fact: CO2 capture rate is an explicit monitoring parameter.
facts.expected_handling: Store measured capture rate with period and method.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring includes verification that the CO2 product is suitable for safe transport and storage.
facts.expected_handling: Attach quality-verification method and destination specification.

facts.source_fact: A monitoring plan is needed for commissioning as well as routine operation.
facts.expected_handling: Version monitoring regime by operating phase.

facts.source_fact: Commissioning is likely to require more extensive monitoring than routine operation.
facts.expected_handling: Do not assume routine frequency during commissioning.

facts.source_fact: Because PCC is an emerging technique, monitoring-method proposals should be included in the permit application.
facts.expected_handling: Require permit-method provenance.

facts.source_fact: Compliance with permit emission limit values must be demonstrated by monitoring authorised release points.
facts.expected_handling: Bind measurements to authorised release points and ELVs.

facts.source_fact: The process must be managed to prevent or minimise solvent degradation products.
facts.expected_handling: Track degradation-control monitoring separately.

facts.source_fact: Point-source monitoring includes ammonia, volatile solvent components and likely degradation products such as nitrosamines and nitramines.
facts.expected_handling: Keep analyte identity and method with each result.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring can use continuous emissions monitoring or periodic extractive sampling depending on the parameter and conditions.
facts.expected_handling: Store monitoring mode and averaging basis.

facts.source_fact: Where aerosol formation is expected, periodic extractive sampling must be isokinetic.
facts.expected_handling: Require isokinetic-method evidence for aerosol cases.

facts.source_fact: CO2 monitoring should include mass balance, CO2 in fuel, capture rate, CO2 released and CO2 quality.
facts.expected_handling: Keep mass-balance components traceable rather than one unsupported net figure.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring should be performed by competent personnel using recognised standards such as MCERTS, or equivalent certified evidence.
facts.expected_handling: Carry competence and certification provenance.

facts.source_fact: Laboratory analysis for monitoring must use a UKAS-accredited laboratory under the guidance.
facts.expected_handling: Require accreditation evidence with laboratory results.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach PCC process, release point, analyte, operating phase and permit boundary.
Carry sampling mode, MCERTS/UKAS, modelling and mass-balance provenance.
Do not convert PCC installation monitoring into parcel-level measured emissions.
